r: CPE 1040 surveys a cross-section of computer-engineering subfields, teaches the design process and teamwork, and has students use math and computer programs to analyze raw data and present results to peers. Mapped to O*NET, the applied activities are Getting Information, Analyzing Data or Information, and Thinking Creatively about designs, alongside team communication. Execution pieces such as calculation, plotting, and slide drafting are exposed, and observed-usage data shows Computer and Mathematical work is the largest AI-usage category. But design framing and career orientation fall in the lower-exposure critical-thinking band that task-exposure research finds negatively associated with automation. The binding constraint is structural: this is foundational scaffolding for the ABET-accredited computer-engineering sequence, whose math/science and engineering-topic credit-hour floors mandate an introductory grounding. At 24 months the instrumental need to acquire early engineering orientation and problem-framing is essentially untouched; AI assists the arithmetic, not the disciplinary onboarding. Rating Low.

By 2031, AI will readily handle the introductory data-analysis, computation, and presentation-drafting tasks the course exercises, and productivity evidence such as GitHub Copilot's measured task speedups and large writing-time reductions confirms these preparatory activities compress sharply. The instrumental case erodes toward design judgment and the ability to frame and verify engineering problems, competencies that grow more valuable as AI generates candidate solutions of uneven quality, the jagged-frontier concern. Yet foundational scaffolding caps the erosion: every downstream computer-engineering course assumes this orientation, and the ABET content-hour floors keep an introductory engineering course structurally required across a catalog revision cycle. The rating rises to Medium, not High, because the substrate role and accreditation lock both bind. A student still needs this grounding to supervise AI-assisted engineering work rather than being displaced from acquiring it; the tools change, the onboarding requirement holds firmly across this horizon.

A decade out, AI will be woven through engineering workflows, absorbing routine calculation, documentation, and preliminary design exploration in the central case. Introductory execution is largely automatable, so the pure task rationale weakens. But engineering judgment, framing problems, specifying constraints, and verifying that an AI-generated design is safe and sound, remains a necessary human competence, and this course scaffolds it while ABET's mandated content floors persist absent accreditor change. Capability-trend evidence points to fast growth, yet diffusion data shows adoption lagging capability unevenly, so I hedge against a confident point-prediction. The rating holds Medium, capped by foundational role and institutional lock-in from reaching High. The genuine uncertainty concerns how first-year engineering is taught and practiced under pervasive AI, not whether an introductory grounding remains instrumentally necessary for students entering the accredited computer-engineering program, which in the central case it does.
CPE 1040.d: This course is an introductory engineering course exposing students to a cross section of topics in computer engineering discipline to assist them with their education career choices. Students are taught to work in teams, introduced to the design process, utilize math and computer programs to analyze raw data and properly display their results in a presentation to their peers. The history of the engineering profession and its relation to current national, social, industrial, ethical, and international issues and problems will be discussed.

CPE 3400.d: This course provides an introduction to the student to the basic concepts of signals and system modeling. The students will develop and understand time-domain and frequency-domain analysis of both continuous and discrete systems and signals.

CPE 3500.d: Students develop an understanding of semiconductor physics, materials, devices and fabrication technology. The students learn semiconductor band theory, semiconductor materials and statistics, heterojunction, Schottky junctions, and MOSFETs. The course focuses on the MOSFET designs for advanced Very Large Scale Integrated Circuit (VLSI) technology from its physical structure, accurate modeling, manufacturability and applications by using computer simulation.

Compensator computation and Bode analysis are exposed to AI, but control reasoning is scientific and safety-critical: verifying a controller's stability margins requires the knowledge itself, and the lab adds partial embodiment of measurement and tuning on real hardware. The binding constraint is foundational and accreditation-based: this is prerequisite scaffolding for CPE 4710 within the ABET-accredited sequence. At 24 months the instrumental need to build control-analysis competence is not eroded; AI can compute a PID gain, but validating that a physical loop is stable and well-behaved is exactly what the course develops through its combined analysis and bench work.

By 2031, AI will fluently perform control analysis, compute compensators, and simulate loop response, eroding the design-by-hand rationale. But control systems fail dangerously and non-obviously, since an unstable loop damages equipment or people, so the verification competence the course builds keeps a knowledgeable human necessary, exactly the jagged-frontier condition where miscalibrated trust in AI output is costly. The laboratory's hands-on tuning and measurement add embodiment that resists full substitution. Foundational scaffolding for digital-control coursework and ABET's engineering-topic hour floors cap the erosion at Medium. The shift is from calculating compensators to specifying, tuning, and confirming that an AI-proposed controller is safe on real hardware, a Medium, not a High, on this horizon.

A decade out, AI will handle control analysis and much compensator design automatically in the central case, and the analytical execution rationale is largely eroded. But control engineering remains partly embodied, instrumenting, measuring, and troubleshooting real loops, and verifying that AI-designed controllers are stable and safe against physical behavior requires the foundational competence this course builds, while ABET content structures persist. Capability trends point to fast progress, yet safety-critical verification is the durable human residue task-exposure and jagged-frontier evidence both emphasize, so I hedge against a confident 2036 prediction. The rating holds Medium, capped by foundational role and verification burden from reaching High. CPE 3715.d: This course analyzes classical, linear, continuous-time control systems. Analysis and design will be done using Laplace transforms, Bode plots. Topics discussed include: stability, transient response, steady-state response, and the design of P, Pl, PD, and PID, Lag and Lead compensators. The laboratory section of the course uses the classical approach to the analysis and design of control systems.

CPE 4020.d: Students in this course will learn a Hardware Description Language (HDL) which is used to design and simulate very large scale digital integrated circuits. Different modeling and design approaches will be covered as well as different simulation techniques.
